title: Level 2 (Intermediate) - D-28
notes:
West leads the ♣K against 4♠. Dummy's ♣A wins the first trick and the contract looks very secure with only 3 losers in diamonds. The only danger is that South could lose control of the hand. The actual 4-2 trump break will lead to the defeat of the contract if South is not careful.

Suppose South ruffs a club back to his hand and draws all of the outstanding trumps in 4 rounds. South then starts on diamonds, but East wins the first round and forces South to ruff a heart. West wins the second round of diamonds and forces South's last trump with his club return. South is out of trump and out of tricks. West will win the third round of diamonds, leaving the defense in a position to win the rest of the tricks.

South can avoid this danger by starting on diamonds at trick 2. East wins the first round and forces South to ruff a heart. South continues with 4 rounds of trump followed by a second round of diamonds to West. South can ruff the return and drive out West's last diamond honor. South still has a trump left and he can win West's return and take the last 2 tricks in diamonds.

The recommended line of play only loses when the East-West spades are 3-3 and West was dealt the ♦AKQx(x), or if East holds those diamonds which is rather unlikely in view of his pre-emptive 4♥ opening. West would certainly select a diamond as his opening lead with the ♦AKQ so, as a practical matter, the recommended line can only gain. Furthermore, the recommended line is necessary given the actual 4-2 spade break.
